I always buy the Pilot G2 Gel Ink pens, and for good reason: they work great. They write smoothly and clearly. I only recently recently discovered that there are subtle differences among the numbers for these pens, however. For example, I usually buy the "07" version of the pen, but the last time I tried the "05" wondering what the difference was. Apparently, the lower the number, the finer the point of the pen.

For my uses, the "05" (Fine point) was just too small of a point; it was a bit more difficult to write with and the lines were obviously thinner. Therefore, I went back to the "07" (Medium point).

I generally don't use these too much in a given day so they tend to last me a while. However, for a more moderate user (someone who uses pens just about every day, but does not write too much at a time) they will last a shorter time. Of course, the best way to know for sure is to just try them out and see for yourself.

The gel flow of this pen is my favorite by far. It leaves a smooth trail of ink, unlike the typical non-gel ink pen that tends to skip a few portions of each letter while composing your masterpiece to show Hemingway how story writing's really done (not Earnest, but rather that guy next to your desk). Yet, this pen does not leave a messy trail of wet ink; if you tend to dwell or doze off while writing, it won't leave a blotch of ink through your entire notebook.

The ink cartridge is also replaceable, but I personally don't think it's worth the hassle/cost (recyclable?).

I usually love 0.5mm tip size to make sense of my messy handwriting (was that a "c" or an "e"?), but 0.7mm is great to give depth to your handwriting (nice thickness, provided you have decent handwriting).

The only downside to this pen is that since it's gel-based, it tends to rub off smooth surfaces. For typical paper, this pen is PERFECT. However, for smooth or laminated paper--like labels or back of photos--you should opt for a regular, non-gel, Bic-type or felt-tip pen.

2) They come in bulk (a dozen), and I use a lot, so it's a cost savings and also convenient. As you can see from the picture, cutting the top off the box makes for an easy little distribution center.
3) The ink distribution is even. These do not blob or skip. That should be a given for every pen in the world, but if you use pens, you know it's never a guarantee. I've never had these pens give anything but a perfect line down to the last drop of ink.
